title: "History and identity"
subtitle: "A name that brings together chemistry, education and curiosity"
---

## The origin of the name

MACEDONIA emerged as a space to **make academic work visible** and **strengthen collaboration networks**. Its name is an acronym formed from the highlighted letters of *química orgánica y educación química* (organic chemistry and chemical education), the two fields that make up its identity:

<p class="acronym-name" lang="es"><span class="visually-hidden">M A C E D O N I A</span><span aria-hidden="true">qui<b>M</b>ica org<b>A</b>ni<b>C</b>a y <b>ED</b>ucaci<b>ON</b> qu<b>I</b>mic<b>A</b></span></p>

<p class="acronym-note">It is written without accent marks on purpose, so that the highlighted letters stand out more.</p>

**M**·**A**·**C**·**E**·**D**·**O**·**N**·**I**·**A**

The choice of name is also linked to an interest in the **history of Greek civilization** and to the **macedonia fruit salad** (*macedonia de frutas*). The latter connects closely and memorably with the studies of antioxidants and free radicals in the team's research. Together, these ideas explain why a chemistry and education laboratory has such an unconventional name.

## An academic trajectory in development

Germán Barriga González joined UMCE in **2017**. This is a milestone in the trajectory, although **it is not a formal founding date of the laboratory**. Within the Department of Chemistry, disciplinary lines, educational projects, student training and academic collaborations have been developed.

::: {.timeline-m}
<div class="timeline-item"><span>2017</span><div><strong>Academic link with UMCE.</strong> Start of Germán Barriga González's academic work at UMCE.</div></div>
<div class="timeline-item"><span>2018–2020</span><div><strong>Disciplinary and educational research.</strong> Projects on organic chemistry, free radicals and online pre-laboratories.</div></div>
<div class="timeline-item"><span>2024–2025</span><div><strong>Modeling and digital fabrication.</strong> Projects on computational chemistry, 3D printing and chemistry learning.</div></div>
<div class="timeline-item"><span>2026</span><div><strong>Continuity of experimental and educational research.</strong> Participation in MAPEX, which studies learning experiences in chemistry laboratories.</div></div>
:::

## An evolving identity

Disciplinary work has included the study of natural and synthetic antioxidant compounds, free radical traps and characterization techniques such as electron spin resonance and computational methods. At the same time, educational research has addressed initial teacher education, laboratory interactions, inclusion and the use of technologies for learning science.

Today these strands are also expressed in developments in **simulation, molecular modeling and 3D printing**, which connect chemistry with new pedagogical possibilities. This is an expansion of the lines of work, not a replacement of their origin.
